question: Compare the meaning of 'sample' in statistics and in machine learning.
answer: It is not the same as measurement precision in statistics. sample: in machine learning a sample usually means one row of data (one example). [S5] In statistics a sample is a subset of a population. bias: the error from wrong assumptions of a model. [S5]

citations.title: Ml Notation Abbreviations
citations.text: OOB: out-of-bag. In a random forest each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample, and the rows left out of that sample are the out-of-bag rows; about 36.8% (1/e) of the rows are out-of-bag for each tree. They provide a free validation estimate. MAE: mean absolute error. RMSE: root mean squared error. SGD: stochastic gradient descent. k-NN: k-nearest neighbors. PR AUC: area under the precision-recall curve; preferred over ROC AUC for strongly imbalanced classes. i.i.d.: independent and identically distributed. precision: in classification, TP / (TP + FP). It is not the same as measurement precision in statistics. sample: in machine learning a sample usually means one row of data (one example). In statistics a sample is a subset of a population. bias: the error from wrong assumptions of a model. The bias term (intercept) of a linear model is a different thing.

S3.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
S3.text:
3. The Bootstrap
The bootstrap estimates the uncertainty of a statistic by resampling. Draw n observations with
replacement from the original sample of size n, compute the statistic, and repeat this B times, for
example B = 1000. The spread of the B statistics approximates the sampling variability.
A bootstrap percentile interval for 95% confidence uses the 2.5th and the 97.5th percentiles of the
B bootstrap statistics. The bootstrap needs no formula for the standard error, which makes it useful
for medians and other awkward statistics.
